questions.question: Which ancient civilization lived along the Nile River and built the Great Sphinx?
questions.explanation: The ancient Egyptians lived along the Nile River and built monuments like the Sphinx and the Pyramids.
questions.funFact: The Great Sphinx is a massive statue with the body of a lion and the head of a human!

questions.question: What famous ancient trade route connected China to Europe?
questions.explanation: The Silk Road was a network of trade routes where merchants traded silk, spices, and other goods.
questions.funFact: It wasn't a single road, but a massive web of trails stretching over 4,000 miles!

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington led the Continental Army during the Revolutionary War and became the first U.S. President.
questions.funFact: George Washington never actually lived in the White House; it was built after his presidency!

questions.question: Which ancient empire built a vast network of roads and huge water bridges called aqueducts?
questions.explanation: The Romans were incredible engineers who built roads and aqueducts that spread across Europe.
questions.funFact: Some of the Roman aqueducts built over 2,000 years ago are still in use today!

questions.question: What was the name of the ship that brought the Pilgrims to America in 1620?
questions.explanation: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrims from England to what is now Massachusetts.
questions.funFact: The Mayflower journey took 66 days, and the ship was very crowded, carrying 102 passengers!

questions.question: Which wealthy African king from the Mali Empire is often considered the richest person in history?
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa ruled the Mali Empire, which was rich in gold and salt.
questions.funFact: On his journey to Mecca, he gave away so much gold that he actually lowered its value in Egypt for over ten years!

questions.question: Who invented the printing press in the 1400s, changing how books were made?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg invented the movable type printing press, allowing books to be printed quickly instead of copied by hand.
questions.funFact: Before the printing press, a single book could take months or even years to write by hand!

questions.question: Which ancient civilization built the city of Machu Picchu high in the Andes Mountains?
questions.explanation: The Incas built Machu Picchu in Peru without using any wheels or iron tools.
questions.funFact: The stones of Machu Picchu fit together so perfectly that you can't even slide a piece of paper between them!

questions.question: What is the name of the oldest known writing system, invented in Mesopotamia using wedge-shaped marks?
questions.explanation: Cuneiform was invented by the Sumerians and was written on clay tablets using a stylus.
questions.funFact: It was used to keep track of trade, like how many sheep or bushels of grain someone owned!

questions.question: During the Middle Ages, what serious disease spread across Europe along trade routes?
questions.explanation: The Black Death, or bubonic plague, was a terrible sickness that affected millions of people in the 1300s.
questions.funFact: People thought the disease was spread by 'bad air,' so plague doctors wore masks stuffed with sweet-smelling flowers!

questions.question: Which famous explorer is credited with completing the first circumnavigation (sailing all the way around) of the globe?
questions.explanation: Magellan's expedition was the first to sail entirely around the world, though Magellan himself died during the journey.
questions.funFact: Magellan named the Pacific Ocean 'Pacific' because the waters seemed very peaceful and calm to him!

questions.question: What famous document signed in 1776 declared the American colonies independent from Great Britain?
questions.explanation: The Declaration of Independence announced that the thirteen colonies were a new nation.
questions.funFact: Two of the signers, Thomas Jefferson and John Adams, both died on the exact same day: July 4, 1826!

questions.question: In ancient Greece, what city-state was famous for its fierce warriors and military training?
questions.explanation: Sparta was a warrior society where boys left home at age 7 to start military training.
questions.funFact: Spartan soldiers wore bright red cloaks to hide the blood if they were injured in battle!

questions.question: Who was the brave young woman who led the French army to victory during the Hundred Years' War?
questions.explanation: Joan of Arc was a peasant girl who believed she had visions telling her to help the French king defeat the English.
questions.funFact: She was only a teenager when she led the army into battle!

questions.question: What period in history saw a huge shift from making things by hand to making them with machines in factories?
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution started in the 1700s and changed how people lived, worked, and traveled.
questions.funFact: The invention of the steam engine was a massive part of this, powering everything from trains to factory looms!

questions.question: Which famous artist and inventor from the Renaissance painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci was a true 'Renaissance Man' who painted, sculpted, and sketched early ideas for flying machines.
questions.funFact: Leonardo often wrote his notes backwards, so they could only be read if you held them up to a mirror!

questions.question: What was the name of the first artificial satellite sent into space in 1957?
questions.explanation: Sputnik 1 was launched by the Soviet Union, kicking off the 'Space Race' between the US and the USSR.
questions.funFact: Sputnik was only about the size of a beach ball, but it terrified people who could hear it beeping on the radio!

questions.question: Who was the Egyptian queen known for her intelligence and alliances with Roman leaders Julius Caesar and Mark Antony?
questions.explanation: Cleopatra was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt.
questions.funFact: Although she ruled Egypt, Cleopatra was actually of Greek descent!

questions.question: What famous massive ship sank on its first voyage in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
questions.explanation: The RMS Titanic was considered 'unsinkable,' but it tragically sank in the North Atlantic Ocean.
questions.funFact: The Titanic had its own swimming pool, a squash court, and a gym with an electric horse!

questions.question: Which ancient civilization developed the concept of the number zero and built huge step pyramids in Central America?
questions.explanation: The Maya were brilliant astronomers and mathematicians who lived in parts of what is now Mexico and Central America.
questions.funFact: The Maya played a ball game where players couldn't use their hands or feet, only their hips and knees!
